tasks.title: Dev servers survive dashboard restarts on Windows
tasks.notes: When the dashboard API restarts (server/scripts/dev.mjs kills it with TerminateProcess on Windows), dev servers started from the Dev tab keep running orphaned and hold their ports. Remember their PIDs and stop or re-adopt them on startup.

reviewer.summary: Recording running dev servers to data/dev-servers.json and stopping their surviving process trees on startup works for the normal Windows restart. But the PID-reuse check only requires children to have started after the recorded start time, so after a reboot or a long outage it can match and taskkill unrelated processes. The Unix path is mostly a no-op.

findings.text: If the recorded top process is gone, leftoverTree accepts any process whose parent ID is the recorded PID and that started after the recorded startedAt. Windows keeps the parent ID of processes whose parent has exited, so after a reboot (or a long outage after the dashboard was killed outright) an unrelated tree whose dead parent reused that PID passes the check and gets taskkill /T /F'd. Example: Explorer, whose launching parent exits right away. First-level children of a dead top process should be bounded to a short window after startedAt, and the cleanup should be skipped if the machine booted after startedAt.

On Unix, killTree(r.pid) only runs when leftoverTree found something. Once the shell leader has exited, its children are reparented to PID 1 and nothing is found, so the surviving process group is never killed, despite the comment. On macOS, `ps -o etimes=` isn't supported, so the process table is empty and the cleanup never runs.
processTable() runs PowerShell Get-CimInstance synchronously while the module loads (20 s timeout), which blocks API startup whenever leftovers were recorded.

tasks.title: Tighten PID-reuse check when stopping leftover dev servers
tasks.notes: In leftoverTree (server/src/lib/devServers.ts), when the recorded top process is no longer running, only accept direct children that started within ~60 s after the recorded startedAt. Also skip all records if the machine booted after startedAt (Win32_OperatingSystem.LastBootUpTime, or /proc/uptime). This stops taskkill /T /F from hitting unrelated processes that reused the PID after a reboot or long outage.

tasks.title: Make leftover dev-server cleanup work on Unix
tasks.notes: stopLeftovers in server/src/lib/devServers.ts only kills the process group if leftoverTree finds a live process, but orphaned children are reparented to PID 1 and macOS ps has no etimes. Look up surviving members by process group ID (ps -o pid=,pgid=,etime=) and kill the group when any member matches the recorded start time.

tasks.title: Re-adopt dev servers across dashboard restarts
tasks.notes: Dev servers are now killed on restart because their output pipes die with the API. Write each dev server's stdout/stderr to a log file in data/ instead of pipes, then on startup reattach to the surviving PID (tail the log, watch the process) instead of killing it. That way a dashboard restart doesn't take down the user's dev server. Code: startDevServer and stopLeftovers in server/src/lib/devServers.ts.
